content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to capture 40 inputs using a [product_name] PLC, but its maximum is 20 inputs. Is it possible to use two [product_name] units, connect them together, and display everything on a single operator panel? I'd like to keep costs low since the PLC just needs to record alarm inputs and show them on the panel. Our old [company_name] PLC with serial display is out of service. Any ideas?
Can you provide some details on how to do this? I suppose it’s straightforward.
Hi, please refer to this related forum topic: [url]
Which [product_name] software version are you using?

The latest [product_name] model supports the following: - 24 digital inputs - 20 digital outputs - 8 analog inputs - 8 analog outputs A possible solution is: One master [product_name] with display plus two digital expansion modules, providing 24 digital inputs. One slave [product_name] without display plus two digital expansion modules, offering another 24 digital inputs. This setup offers 48 digital inputs, leaving some reserve inputs available. With master-slave communication, the main logic resides in the master [product_name], while the slave supplies only its I/O to the master.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants examined input limitations of [product_name] PLC devices and discussed ways to increase the number of inputs by networking devices and adding expansion modules. The solution revolves around using a master-slave arrangement and expansions to boost available inputs, ensuring alarm signals can be centrally shown with minimal expense.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for an affordable method to capture more than 20 digital inputs, ideally managed through a single operator panel, using interconnected [product_name] devices or expansion modules.
